record.original_question: Is the observed Higgs boson h an elementary scalar field, or is it a composite state, for example a pseudo-Goldstone boson emerging from a strongly interacting sector? If h is composite, can Higgs-coupling measurements reveal the relevant compositeness parameters, such as the resonance mass scale mρ, the resonance coupling gρ, and the dimensionless combination ξ = gρ²v²/mρ²?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Standard Model Higgs boson h, a neutral scalar with vacuum expectation value v ≈ 246 GeV. Two hypotheses are entertained:

(a) h is a fundamental elementary scalar field.

(b) h is a composite bound state arising as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of a spontaneously broken global symmetry of a new strongly interacting sector. In the Strongly Interacting Light Higgs (SILH) effective field theory framework, the low-energy Lagrangian for such a composite Higgs depends, to leading order, on two parameters:
   • mρ, the mass scale of the resonances of the strong sector,
   • gρ ∈ (0, 4π], the typical coupling of those resonances,
together with the dimensionless compositeness parameter
   ξ := gρ² v² / mρ².
The SILH Lagrangian predicts deviations of the Higgs couplings to Standard Model particles (e.g. to W, Z, top, bottom, photons, gluons) from their Standard Model values, with the leading deviations being functions of ξ (and, at next order, of the ratio v/mρ and gρ).

Problem. 
(1) Determine whether h is elementary or composite.
(2) Assuming h is composite in the SILH sense, decide whether precision measurements of Higgs couplings — i.e. the set of ratios κi = gi^obs / gi^SM for i ranging over Standard Model particles coupling to the Higgs — suffice to identify the underlying compositeness parameters mρ, gρ, and ξ. Specifically, exhibit an explicit map from a finite set of measurable Higgs coupling ratios {κi} to (mρ, gρ, ξ), or prove that such an inversion is obstructed (e.g. by degeneracies in the leading SILH predictions), and quantify the precision required on {κi} to reconstruct ξ within a stated uncertainty.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the observed Higgs boson is elementary or a composite pseudo-Goldstone state remains open. As of recent LHC results (ATLAS and CMS Run 2 combinations), Higgs couplings agree with Standard Model predictions within roughly 10%, placing bounds ξ ≲ 0.1 and pushing mρ above the TeV scale, but no positive determination of compositeness has been made; future colliders (HL-LHC, FCC-ee, ILC) are projected to probe ξ down to the 10⁻³–10⁻² level.

status_evidence.title: Composite Higgs review (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Composite Higgs models remain a viable alternative to elementary Higgs scenarios; current LHC data constrain but do not exclude them.
status_evidence.claim: The elementary-vs-composite Higgs question is still open and constrained by but not resolved by current data.

status_evidence.title: ATLAS/CMS Higgs coupling measurements
status_evidence.snippet: Measured Higgs coupling modifiers are consistent with Standard Model predictions within current uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: No deviation from elementary Higgs behavior has been observed, leaving compositeness parameters unconstrained at small ξ.
